items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: Madeline Green come in with a major in the Army. That was the singer in the group

ctx.x: there and myself and Leo and we never got served, and everybody come around because they thought all of us was Black. And they had a sign on there, "We reserve the right to refuse anyone service," during the war days.

So what we did, we laughed about it, but Madeline Green come in with a major in the Army. That was the singer in the group, and they went in the back to eat, and they were served before we got served, and here was a social worker in the place, and we went back to tell Madeline what happened at the bar. We never got served. We were between breaks on shows.

Everybody that come after us was served. So we told Madeline -- the social worker was there to witness it -- so we went to Gladys, and Gladys got the theater manager, and we filed a claim against Leo Poole's bar, and it cost me and Herbie $17.50 a piece, $35.00, and we said, we can't appear in court. The lawyer said, don't worry about. We got $100.00 for that situation. We turned it over to the NAACP.
